# Macro-event TQQQ: the FOMC intermeeting drift

**Development window:** 2016-01-04 -> 2023-12-29. 1-minute marks, next-open
fills, 2% band, long-only, weights >= 0 and sum <= 1. **No 2024+ data was
loaded by this study.**

**Verdict:** the strategy **passes the literal development gate** (51.06% CAGR
vs 36.72%, 48.83% max DD vs 82.29%) at 1, 5 and 10 bp. It is **not robust to
dropping 2020**: the ex-2020 CAGR is about 33.4%, below the bar, and 2016-2019
also lags TQQQ. The honest reading is a genuine risk-adjusted improvement
(Sharpe 1.17 vs 0.82, Calmar 1.05 vs 0.44) whose CAGR edge is concentrated in
the 2020 and 2022 regimes.

---

## 1. Headline

| | CAGR | max DD | Sharpe | Sortino | vol | TQQQ exposure | fills | turnover |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| **Primary, 1 bp** | **51.06%** | **48.83%** | **1.17** | 1.67 | 43.3% | **55.8%** | 253 | 2,079x |
| Primary, 5 bp | 49.16% | 49.08% | 1.14 | 1.63 | 43.3% | 55.8% | 253 | 1,929x |
| Primary, 10 bp | 46.81% | 49.38% | 1.11 | 1.58 | 43.3% | 55.8% | 253 | 1,758x |
| TQQQ bar (published) | 36.72% | 82.29% | 0.82 | -- | -- | 100% | -- | -- |
| TQQQ recomputed on this panel | 36.15% | 82.29% | 0.80 | -- | 66.6% | 100% | -- | -- |

* Ending equity at 1 bp: **$2.694M** from $100k (25.9x).
* Daily correlation to TQQQ: **0.657**; beta **0.429**. Correlation to QQQ:
  0.653; beta 1.269.
* Max drawdown episode: peak **2021-12-27**, trough **2022-05-24**. Daily-mark
  drawdown is 44.63%; the 1-minute mark is 48.83%.
* The TQQQ benchmark recomputed on the same 1-minute panel is 36.15% / 82.29%
  / 0.80, i.e. 0.57 pp below the published 36.72% CAGR. The program bar is the
  published figure; the comparison is conservative by that amount.

## 2. Exact rules

For every **scheduled FOMC decision day** `F` (63 dates, 2016-2023):

```
long TQQQ from the open of session F+3
through the close of session F+20      (18 sessions)
BIL otherwise
```

* Entry is a target set on the prior session's last bar, filled at the next
  session's 09:30 open.
* Exit is a target set at 15:58 and filled at the 15:59 open, so the position
  is not carried overnight after the window.
* If a window runs past the end of the development sample it is truncated at
  the last available session. That happens once, for the December 2023
  meeting; 62 cycles are complete, 1 is truncated.
* No stop, no trend filter, no volatility target, no shorting, no CPI/OpEx in
  the primary. Weights are 0/1 in TQQQ and the complement in BIL.
* Event count: 63 scheduled meetings; 63 windows (62 complete + 1 truncated).
  TQQQ is held for 55.8% of the 781,880 one-minute bars (2,012 sessions).

The 2020-03-03 and 2020-03-15 emergency meetings are excluded because they
were not knowable in advance. The scheduled 2020-03-18 meeting was cancelled
and is not used; a sensitivity that adds it is in section 6.6.

## 3. Why this window should carry a premium

Scheduled FOMC meetings are the highest-attention macro events on the
calendar. The literature documents two adjacent effects:

1. **Announcement premium.** Lucca & Moench (2015) and Savor & Wilson (2013)
   find excess equity returns in the 24 hours before scheduled FOMC decisions:
   investors pay for protection into the event, and the announcement resolves
   the uncertainty.
2. **FOMC cycle.** Cieslak, Morse & Vissing-Jorgensen (2019) show the equity
   premium is not uniform across the intermeeting period; it is concentrated
   in particular weeks, with flat or negative phases elsewhere.

The development-sample offset profile has a consistent three-phase shape
(TQQQ close-to-close, all 63 meetings, bp):

| phase | sessions | mean TQQQ |
|---|---|---:|
| pre-meeting run-up | -1, 0 | +64.5, +80.8 |
| immediate post-decision | +1, +2 | -76.6, -50.0 |
| intermeeting drift | +3 ... +20 | mostly positive, ~+35/day |
| late pre-meeting | -9 ... -2 | choppy / negative |

The story is: the decision resolves the policy path; the first two days are a
positioning unwind and a pay-back of the announcement premium; capital is then
redeployed over the next three weeks. In the last week before the next meeting
the market de-risks again.

This is an **index-level** effect, not a TQQQ artefact. On QQQ the same
+3...+20 window returns +2.29% per cycle over 62 cycles: **t = 4.03, 74%
positive**. TQQQ is the leveraged implementation; the 3x reset amplifies the
timing alpha.

## 4. Results

### 4.1 Yearly returns

| Year | Strategy | TQQQ | Comment |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| 2016 | +29.7% | +19.9% | beats |
| 2017 | +42.4% | +114.5% | lags a strong bull |
| 2018 | +8.5% | -20.8% | beats the drawdown year |
| 2019 | +72.2% | +148.2% | lags |
| 2020 | +249.3% | +104.1% | the COVID gap and rebound |
| 2021 | +45.1% | +81.1% | lags |
| 2022 | -8.5% | -79.4% | the main risk-management year |
| 2023 | +61.2% | +192.0% | lags the AI bull |

The profile is consistent: the strategy wins in flat/down years and loses in
strong bull years. It is not a bull-market replacement.

### 4.2 Subperiods

| Period | Strategy CAGR / DD / Sharpe | TQQQ CAGR (approx.) |
|---|---:|---:|
| 2016-2019 | 35.36% / 44.96% / 0.99 | 38.2% |
| 2020-2021 | 126.64% / 35.90% / 2.20 | 92.3% |
| 2022-2023 | 22.94% / 47.98% / 0.65 | -22.4% |

The strategy lags TQQQ in the calm 2016-2019 bull, then beats by a wide margin
in the two crisis regimes. That is the whole source of the full-window pass.

### 4.3 Drawdown

The 48.83% 1-minute drawdown runs from the 2021-12-27 peak to the 2022-05-24
trough. It is not a single bad close: the strategy is long 100% TQQQ inside a
window, so an intra-window crash is taken in full. The worst complete cycles
were:

| FOMC | window | TQQQ |
|---|---|---:|
| 2018-09-26 | 2018-10-01 -> 2018-10-24 | -32.75% |
| 2020-01-29 | 2020-02-03 -> 2020-02-27 | -20.52% |
| 2019-05-01 | 2019-05-06 -> 2019-05-30 | -16.68% |
| 2022-01-26 | 2022-01-31 -> 2022-02-24 | -12.89% |
| 2023-07-26 | 2023-07-31 -> 2023-08-23 | -12.22% |

The best cycles were 2020-06-10 (+42.65%), 2018-12-19 (+40.64%),
2020-09-16 (+35.37%), 2022-11-02 (+30.51%) and 2023-05-03 (+28.24%).

## 5. Event evidence

### 5.1 Per-cycle distribution

| | n | mean | median | sd | t | positive |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| TQQQ | 62 | +6.33% | +5.71% | 14.01% | **3.55** | 71.0% |
| QQQ | 62 | +2.29% | +2.16% | 4.47% | **4.03** | 74.2% |

The QQQ result is the more important number: the same 18-session window earns
a significant positive return in the unlevered index, so the strategy is not
a TQQQ-specific curve fit. It is a calendar premium implemented with leverage.

### 5.2 Offset profile

Key offsets (TQQQ close-to-close, bp, 63 events; standard errors are roughly
40-60 bp, so individual cells are noisy):

| offset | -5 | -3 | -2 | -1 | **0** | +1 | +2 | +3 | +4 | +5 | +10 | +14 | +20 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| mean | +95.6 | -22.7 | -19.8 | +64.5 | **+80.8** | -76.6 | -50.0 | +51.5 | +56.0 | -1.6 | -0.9 | +109.2 | +43.5 |

The three-phase shape is visible, but the individual cells are noisy. The
robust part is the cycle-level result and the QQQ replication, not any single
offset.

### 5.3 Turn-of-month is not the explanation

A first-three-sessions-of-month TQQQ strategy (14.2% exposure) returns only
4.04% CAGR with a 42.05% DD. The FOMC window is not a repackaged turn of the
month.

## 6. Robustness

### 6.1 Pre-registered grid (8 cells, 1 bp)

| cell | FOMC window | extra | CAGR | max DD | Sharpe | exposure |
|---|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| **G1 (primary)** | **+3...+20** | -- | **51.06%** | **48.83%** | **1.17** | 55.8% |
| G2 | +1...+15 | -- | 23.27% | 47.31% | 0.72 | 46.7% |
| G3 | +3...+15 | -- | 37.11% | 35.72% | 1.04 | 40.4% |
| G4 | +3...+25 | -- | 52.87% | 63.04% | 1.11 | 71.2% |
| G5 | +5...+20 | -- | 36.57% | 55.96% | 0.97 | 49.5% |
| G6 | +3...+20 | CPI [-1,+2] | 40.22% | 70.33% | 0.94 | 63.7% |
| G7 | +3...+20 | OpEx [+1,+3] | **61.42%** | **47.78%** | **1.27** | 61.8% |
| G8 | +3...+20 | CPI + OpEx | 50.31% | 68.08% | 1.06 | 69.2% |

Six of eight cells clear the literal bar; G2 fails and G5 is 0.15 pp short.
The plateau is broad in CAGR but not in drawdown: G4, G6 and G8 have 63-70%
drawdowns, above the 60% ideal.

**G7 is the strongest cell** (61.42% / 47.78% / 1.27 at 1 bp; 54.08% / 48.72%
/ 1.17 at 10 bp). It is not the deliverable because G1 was fixed as the
primary before the final run. Switching to G7 after seeing the grid would be
exactly the post-hoc selection the protocol forbids. G7 is a legitimate
follow-up candidate and is consistent with the existing OpEx literature
(post-expiry sessions are positive). It also contradicts the pre-run
expectation in `HYPOTHESIS.md` that CPI/OpEx additions would only add
drawdown: the post-OpEx sleeve is the one addition that improved both CAGR and
DD.

### 6.2 Random-date placebo (500 draws)

Same event count (63) and hold length (18 sessions), random start sessions;
overlaps allowed, so the median exposure is 43.1% versus the primary's 55.8%.

| | median | p90 | p95 | p99 | max | primary | percentile |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| CAGR | 16.1% | 33.1% | 37.7% | 46.0% | 48.1% | 51.06% | 100.0% |
| max DD | 68.9% | -- | -- | -- | -- | 48.83% | 93.8% better |
| Sharpe | 0.57 | -- | 1.01 | -- | 1.28 | 1.17 | 98.8% |

No random calendar beats the primary on CAGR; the joint fraction with
CAGR >= 51.06% **and** DD <= 48.83% is **0 / 500**.

Because random windows overlap, their exposure is lower. The next placebo
fixes that.

### 6.3 Exposure-matched phase placebo (30 phases)

A generic 30-session cycle with a random phase, 63 non-overlapping 18-session
windows (median exposure 56.4%, close to the primary's 55.8%):

* CAGR: median 16.6%, p90 32.4%, p95 34.8%, max 38.5%; primary 51.06%;
  percentile 100.
* max DD: median 68.5%, best 59.6%; primary 48.83%; percentile 100.
* Sharpe: median 0.56, p95 0.86, max 0.89; primary 1.17; percentile 100.

No phase of a generic 6-week cycle comes close. The FOMC anchor matters, not
just the 55% duty cycle.

### 6.4 Shifted calendar

All FOMC dates shifted by N sessions, same 18-session hold:

| shift | -8 | -6 | -4 | -2 | -1 | **0** | +1 | +2 | +4 | +6 | +8 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| CAGR | 15.1% | 18.9% | 25.6% | 31.4% | 41.1% | **50.6%** | 40.5% | 38.2% | 44.9% | 34.6% | 31.8% |
| max DD | 65.6% | 61.1% | 48.2% | 55.8% | 52.6% | **48.8%** | 56.0% | 59.9% | 57.6% | 79.3% | 86.5% |

The peak is at shift 0. There is a +/-4-session neighbourhood at 38-45%, and
the curve collapses beyond +/-6. The event window is not a one-day spike, but
the exact alignment is load-bearing. (Shift 0 is 50.6%, not 51.06%, because the
shift test requires a full 18-session window and drops the truncated December
2023 window.)

### 6.5 Leave-one-year-out

| dropped year | year return | ex-year CAGR |
|---|---:|---:|
| 2016 | +29.7% | 54.2% |
| 2017 | +44.9% | 51.8% |
| 2018 | +10.2% | 57.9% |
| 2019 | +61.7% | 49.5% |
| **2020** | **+258.6%** | **33.4%** |
| 2021 | +46.7% | 51.6% |
| 2022 | -7.1% | 61.8% |
| 2023 | +64.7% | 49.1% |

Dropping any year except 2020 leaves CAGR at 49-62%, comfortably above the
bar. Dropping 2020 takes it to 33.4%, below the bar. The pass is therefore
**not broad-based enough** to call the strategy robust.

### 6.6 Cancelled March 2020 meeting

Adding the cancelled 2020-03-18 scheduled date (window 2020-03-23 -> 2020-04-17)
gives **62.87% CAGR / 48.83% DD / 1.30 Sharpe**. The primary's choice to exclude
the cancelled meeting is conservative, not result-enhancing.

### 6.7 Costs

The strategy trades 253 fills and 2,079x initial-equity turnover over 8 years
(about 260x/year), because every switch liquidates BIL and buys TQQQ. The cost
drag from 1 to 10 bp is 4.25 pp of CAGR, but the 10 bp result (46.81%) still
clears the bar. Costs are not the failure mode.

## 7. Where it fails

1. **Small sample.** 63 scheduled meetings, 62 complete cycles, 8 per year.
   The cycle-level t-stat is 3.55, but the observations are clustered in time;
   the effective sample is small and the 2020 observations are extreme.
2. **Regime change.** The strategy lags TQQQ in 2016-2019 (35.4% vs ~38.2%)
   and in every strong bull year (2017, 2019, 2021, 2023). The full-window
   pass comes from 2020 (+249%) and 2022 (-8.5% vs -79.4%). Ex-2020 CAGR is
   33.4%, below the bar. A return to a low-volatility bull market with no
   crash would likely underperform buy-and-hold.
3. **The 2020 calendar accident.** The January 2020 window ended on
   2020-02-27; the next scheduled window (April 29 +3) began on 2020-05-04.
   The strategy was therefore flat through the COVID crash. A real-time
   investor knew that schedule, so this is not look-ahead, but it is a one-off
   alignment of the crash with the intermeeting gap. Adding the cancelled
   2020-03-18 date actually *raises* CAGR to 62.87% (the window starts near the
   bottom), so the exclusion is not what creates the pass; the gap alignment
   is still a single historical accident.
4. **Intra-window crash risk.** The strategy is 100% TQQQ inside a window and
   takes the full 2018 Q4 (-32.75%) and 2020 February (-20.52%) cycles. The
   max DD is 48.8%, better than TQQQ's 82.3% but still large. No stop is used;
   adding one would be a different strategy.
5. **Selection disclosure.** The +3/+20 boundaries came from a coarse
   development-sample offset scan, not from a blind theory. The grid is a
   plateau test, but the primary is at the high end of that plateau. The exact
   phase is sample-specific: the literature's "even weeks" pattern does not
   match this sample's phase, and the mechanism story is partly post-hoc.
6. **Possible confounds.** The window may proxy for month-end, OpEx-week or
   other calendar effects. The shift test and the phase placebo argue against
   a generic 6-week cycle and against turn-of-month, but they cannot rule out
   every confound.

## 8. Difference from the existing research

| | `agents2/event-risk-overlay` | `revisit` expiry cycle | this |
|---|---|---|---|
| Base | 165-day QQQ SMA + 4% stop | none | none |
| Exposure | ~100% TQQQ minus one session | own the OpEx cycle, flat expiry | 55.8% TQQQ, FOMC phase only |
| Event | OpEx intraday de-risk | monthly OpEx | scheduled FOMC |
| Timing | overlay on a trend strategy | avoid the weak expiry session | hold the middle of the intermeeting period |
| Dev result | 67.1% / 40.7% on its 2017-2026 10y window | 26.94% / 39.04% | 51.06% / 48.83% |

The original overlay de-risks *one event session* on top of a trend base; the
standalone expiry rebuild owns the OpEx cycle and avoids the expiry session.
This study has no price-based base, holds only in a multi-week phase, and its
premium comes from the phase, not from avoiding a single print. It is not a
copy or a variant of the 165-SMA + 4%-stop strategy.

## 9. Verdict

* **Literal development gate: PASS.** 51.06% CAGR > 36.72%; 48.83% max DD <
  82.29%; 1, 5 and 10 bp all pass.
* **Risk-adjusted: genuine improvement.** Sharpe 1.17 vs 0.82; Calmar 1.05 vs
  0.44; 0.657 correlation and 0.43 beta to TQQQ.
* **Robustness gate: FAIL.** Ex-2020 CAGR 33.4%; 2016-2019 CAGR 35.4%; the
  pass is concentrated in crisis years and in a calendar accident.
* **Use:** a satellite or crisis-hedged TQQQ allocation, not a standalone
  replacement. The FOMC phase effect is strong enough to deserve a follow-up
  with a longer history (pre-2016) and an explicit test of the phase stability.
  G7 (FOMC + post-OpEx) is the best grid cell and the natural next
  pre-registration, but it was not selected here.

## 10. Reproduction

```powershell
cd C:\Users\27175\Desktop\quant-trader-research
$env:PYTHONPATH = "C:\Users\27175\AppData\Local\Temp\opencode\pylibs"
$env:BT_THREADS = "1"
python research/new/macro-event-tqqq/strategy.py
```

`strategy.py` loads
`bt.panel(("QQQ","TQQQ","BIL"), "2016-01-04", "2023-12-29", "1min",
warmup_days=10)`. The last bar is 2023-12-29 15:59; no 2024+ row is read.
`result.json` contains the full grid, placebo distributions, shift curve,
subperiod cuts, leave-one-year-out, per-cycle event study and the March 2020
sensitivity.
hypothesis_md:
# Macro-event TQQQ: the FOMC intermeeting drift

**Status: pre-registration.** Development window only:
**2016-01-04 → 2023-12-29**. The 2024-2026 holdout is not loaded by
`strategy.py` and was not inspected. Next-open fills, 2% band, long-only,
weights ≥ 0 and sum ≤ 1. TQQQ bar: **36.72% CAGR / 82.29% max DD / 0.82
Sharpe** on 1-minute marks.

This is a standalone strategy. It does **not** use the 165-day QQQ SMA, the
4% intraday stop, the old event-risk overlay, or the OpEx-cycle rebuild.

---

## 1. What is different from the existing event work

| | `agents2/event-risk-overlay` | `revisit/event-risk-overlay` (expiry cycle) | this |
|---|---|---|---|
| Base | 165-day QQQ SMA + 4% armed stop | none (calendar only) | none |
| Exposure | ~100% TQQQ except one session | own the OpEx cycle, flat the expiry session | TQQQ only inside FOMC windows |
| Event | OpEx intraday de-risk, FOMC/CPI as controls | monthly OpEx only | scheduled FOMC only |
| Timing | overlay on a trend strategy | flat the weak expiry session | hold the **middle of the intermeeting period** |
| Result | 67.1% / 40.7% on its 2017-2026 10y window (overlay, not standalone) | 26.94% / 39.04% dev, standalone | see `result.json` |

The existing work says *avoid* one event session. This study says the equity
premium is **earned in a specific phase of the FOMC cycle** and is absent in
the adjacent phases. It is a different signal, a different holding pattern and
a different failure mode.

## 2. Mechanism

Scheduled FOMC meetings are the highest-attention macro events on the calendar.
The literature documents two adjacent effects:

1. **Announcement premium.** Lucca & Moench (2015) and Savor & Wilson (2013)
   find excess equity returns in the 24 hours before scheduled FOMC decisions:
   investors pay for protection into the event, and the announcement resolves
   that uncertainty.
2. **FOMC cycle.** Cieslak, Morse & Vissing-Jorgensen (2019) show the equity
   premium is not uniform across the intermeeting period; it is concentrated in
   particular weeks of the cycle, with flat or negative phases elsewhere.

The development-sample offset profile (2016-2023, TQQQ close-to-close, all 63
scheduled meetings) shows a consistent three-phase shape:

| phase | sessions | mean TQQQ | reading |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| pre-meeting run-up | −1, 0 | +64.5, +80.8 bp | announcement premium |
| immediate post-decision | +1, +2 | −76.6, −50.0 bp | positioning unwind / pay-back |
| intermeeting drift | +3 … +20 | positive on most sessions, ~+35 bp/day | risk is redeployed once the path is known |
| late pre-meeting | −9 … −2 | choppy / negative | de-risking into the next meeting |

**H1.** After the two-day post-decision unwind, the policy path is known and
volatility sellers have re-established supply. The equity risk premium is then
earned over the following ~3 weeks. The last week before the next meeting is
de-risking noise and should be avoided.

**H2.** This is an index-level calendar effect, not a TQQQ artefact. On QQQ the
same +3…+20 window returns +2.29% per cycle over 62 cycles (t = 4.03, 74%
positive) — a weaker but highly significant version of the same premium. TQQQ
is the leveraged implementation.

**H3.** Because TQQQ's 3× daily reset suffers volatility drag, being out of the
market during the negative phases (the two post-decision days and the late
pre-meeting week) should improve the *geometric* return even at ~55% exposure.

## 3. Exact rules

Calendar (hardcoded, published by the Fed roughly a year ahead):

* 63 **scheduled** FOMC decision days, 2016-2023, from the Fed's own meeting
  calendars. Unscheduled emergency meetings (2020-03-03, 2020-03-15) are
  excluded because they were not knowable in advance.
* The scheduled March 2020 meeting (2020-03-17/18) was cancelled and replaced
  by the 2020-03-15 emergency decision; it is **not** used as an event. A
  sensitivity that adds 2020-03-18 is reported in `report.md`.
* No CPI, NFP, OpEx or holiday dates are used by the primary. They appear only
  in two pre-registered grid cells as diversifiers.

For each scheduled FOMC decision day `F` (session index `k`):

```
long TQQQ from the open of session k+3
through the close of session k+20   (18 sessions)
BIL otherwise
```

* Entry is a target set on the prior session's last bar and filled at the next
  session's 09:30 open.
* Exit is a target set at 15:58 and filled at the 15:59 open of session k+20,
  so the position is not held overnight after the window.
* If a window would run past the end of the development sample it is truncated
  at the last available session (the December 2023 meeting).
* No stop, no trend filter, no volatility target, no shorting. Weights are
  0/1 in TQQQ and the complement in BIL.

## 4. Why it could beat TQQQ

TQQQ's 36.72% CAGR is bought with an 82.29% drawdown and 0.82 Sharpe. The
strategy holds TQQQ in 55% of sessions but in the phase with the highest
average return and avoids the two worst phases of the cycle. If the phase
effect is real, the geometric return can exceed buy-and-hold despite lower
exposure. The development sample says the held sessions average +35.3 bp/day
(arithmetic) versus +4.2 bp for non-held sessions.

It is still a long-TQQQ strategy: it will lag a strong, low-volatility bull
market, and a crash inside a held window is taken in full.

## 5. Falsifiers (checked in `report.md`)

1. **QQQ check.** The same window on QQQ must show a positive cycle mean with
   t > 1.5 and > 55% positive cycles. Dev: t = 4.03, 74% positive.
2. **Random-date placebo.** 500 random calendars with the same number of events
   (63) and the same 18-session length. The primary should sit above the 95th
   percentile of CAGR and Sharpe and below the 5th percentile of DD.
3. **Shifted calendar.** Shifting every FOMC date by −15…+15 sessions should
   produce a peak at 0; a flat curve would mean the anchor is irrelevant.
4. **Costs.** 10 bp headline must still clear 36.72% CAGR.
5. **Single-year dependence.** Leave-one-year-out. If dropping 2020 collapses
   the CAGR below 36.72%, the pass is a one-regime artefact and must be
   reported as such.
6. **Neighbour grid.** The pass must not be a single-cell spike; the 8-cell
   grid below is reported in full.

## 6. Pre-registered grid (8 cells, 1 bp unless stated)

| cell | FOMC window | extra sleeve | role |
|---|---|---|---|
| **G1 (primary)** | **+3 … +20** | — | mechanism-implied middle of the cycle |
| G2 | +1 … +15 | — | early phase, shorter |
| G3 | +3 … +15 | — | shorter middle |
| G4 | +3 … +25 | — | longer middle, includes late pre-meeting |
| G5 | +5 … +20 | — | later start, more unwind skipped |
| G6 | +3 … +20 | CPI [−1 … +2] | CPI release diversifier |
| G7 | +3 … +20 | OpEx [+1 … +3] | post-expiry flow diversifier |
| G8 | +3 … +20 | CPI + OpEx | all three event families |

The primary is fixed **before** the final run. Cells G2-G8 are a sensitivity
and plateau test, not a selection menu: the report does not switch the primary
to a better neighbour after seeing the results. A coarse offset scan informed
the choice of +3/+20; that is disclosed in `report.md` §7 rather than presented
as blind pre-registration.

CPI dates are the BLS release schedule (2016 dates reconstructed from the
published 2016 schedule; 2017-2023 from archived BLS schedules). OpEx is the
third Friday, holiday-shifted. Neither is used by G1.

## 7. Expected effect (written before the final run)

* Primary: **45-55% CAGR, 45-55% max DD, 1.1-1.2 Sharpe, ~55% TQQQ exposure**.
* Shorter windows: 15-30% CAGR; they miss the drift.
* Longer windows: higher CAGR but DD above 60%.
* CPI/OpEx additions: more exposure, worse drawdown, no improvement in Calmar.
* Placebo median: ~19% CAGR; the primary should be above the 95th percentile.
* Leave-one-year-out: dropping 2020 likely takes CAGR to ~33%, below the bar.
  This is the main honest weakness of the strategy.

spec_md:
## 2. Exact rules

For every **scheduled FOMC decision day** `F` (63 dates, 2016-2023):

```
long TQQQ from the open of session F+3
through the close of session F+20      (18 sessions)
BIL otherwise
```

* Entry is a target set on the prior session's last bar, filled at the next
  session's 09:30 open.
* Exit is a target set at 15:58 and filled at the 15:59 open, so the position
  is not carried overnight after the window.
* If a window runs past the end of the development sample it is truncated at
  the last available session. That happens once, for the December 2023
  meeting; 62 cycles are complete, 1 is truncated.
* No stop, no trend filter, no volatility target, no shorting, no CPI/OpEx in
  the primary. Weights are 0/1 in TQQQ and the complement in BIL.
* Event count: 63 scheduled meetings; 63 windows (62 complete + 1 truncated).
  TQQQ is held for 55.8% of the 781,880 one-minute bars (2,012 sessions).

The 2020-03-03 and 2020-03-15 emergency meetings are excluded because they
were not knowable in advance. The scheduled 2020-03-18 meeting was cancelled
and is not used; a sensitivity that adds it is in section 6.6.

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Calendar and weight construction
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
def _sessions(ts):
    """(dates, first_bar, last_bar, session_dates, day_of) for a 1-min panel."""
    dates = bt.session_dates(ts)
    first, last = bt.day_bounds_from_dates(dates)
    sess = dates[first]
    day_of = {d: k for k, d in enumerate(sess)}
    return dates, first, last, sess, day_of


def event_windows(sess, day_of, events, a_off: int, b_off: int):
    """Inclusive session-index windows ``[k+a_off, k+b_off]`` around events.

    Windows that start before the panel or run past the last session are
    clipped; windows whose event is not a trading day are skipped.
    """
    out = []
    n = len(sess)
    for d in events:
        k = day_of.get(d)
        if k is None:
            continue
        ka, kb = k + a_off, k + b_off
        if ka < 0 or ka >= n:
            continue
        kb = min(kb, n - 1)
        if kb >= ka:
            out.append((ka, kb))
    return out


def weights_from_index_windows(ts, windows):
    """0/1 TQQQ targets from inclusive session windows.

    The target is true from the first bar of the entry session up to (but not
    including) the last bar of the exit session, so the exit fill is the 15:59
    open and the position is not carried overnight after the window.
    """
    dates = bt.session_dates(ts)
    first, last = bt.day_bounds_from_dates(dates)
    target = np.zeros(len(ts), dtype=bool)
    for ka, kb in windows:
        if ka < 0 or kb < ka or ka >= len(first):
            continue
        kb = min(kb, len(first) - 1)
        target[first[ka]:last[kb]] = True
    w = np.zeros((len(ts), 3))
    if len(ts) > 1:
        w[:-1, 1] = target[1:].astype(float)
    w[:, 2] = 1.0 - w[:, 1]
    return w


def build_weights(ts, o, c):
    """Primary strategy weights: FOMC +3 .. +20, TQQQ else BIL.

    Parameters ``o`` and ``c`` are accepted for the shared interface; the
    signal is purely calendar-based and does not use prices.
    """
    _, _, _, sess, day_of = _sessions(ts)
    windows = event_windows(sess, day_of, FOMC_DATES, 3, 20)
    return weights_from_index_windows(ts, windows)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
def _metrics(ts, o, c, w, slip: float = 1.0):
    r = bt.run(ts, o, c, w, START, band=BAND, slippage_bps=slip)
    s = bt.stats(r, BARS_PER_YEAR)
    i = bt.start_index(ts, START)
    eq = np.asarray(r["equity"], dtype=float)
    dts = ts[i:]
    deq = pd.Series(eq, index=dts).groupby(dts.date).last()
    dd_daily = float(-(deq / deq.cummax() - 1.0).min())
    yr = bt.yearly(dts, eq, c[i:, 1])
    years = float(s["years"])
    dd = deq / deq.cummax() - 1.0
    j_dd = int(np.argmin(dd.to_numpy()))
    p_dd = int(np.argmax(deq.to_numpy()[: j_dd + 1]))
    out = {
        "cagr": float(s["cagr"]),
        "total_return": float(s["total_return"]),
        "max_drawdown": float(s["max_drawdown"]),
        "max_drawdown_daily": dd_daily,
        "sharpe": float(s["sharpe"]),
        "sortino": float(s["sortino"]),
        "volatility": float(s["volatility"]),
        "calmar": float(s["cagr"] / s["max_drawdown"]) if s["max_drawdown"] > 0 else None,
        "exposure": float(w[i:, 1].mean()),
        "exposure_invested": float(s["exposure"]),
        "fills": int(s["fills"]),
        "turnover": float(s["turnover"]),
        "turnover_per_year": float(s["turnover"] / years) if years > 0 else None,
        "ending_equity": float(s["ending_equity"]),
        "years": years,
        "dd_peak": str(deq.index[p_dd]),
        "dd_trough": str(deq.index[j_dd]),
        "yearly": {str(k): {"strategy": float(v["strategy"]),
                            "tqqq": float(v["benchmark"])}
                   for k, v in yr.items()},
    }
    return out, eq, dts, deq


def _daily_series(ts, values):
    return pd.Series(values, index=ts).groupby(ts.date).last()


def _corr_beta(ts, equity, price):
    a = _daily_series(ts, equity).pct_change()
    b = _daily_series(ts, price).pct_change()
    j = pd.concat([a.rename("s"), b.rename("b")], axis=1).dropna()
    corr = float(j["s"].corr(j["b"]))
    beta = float(np.cov(j["s"], j["b"])[0, 1] / np.var(j["b"], ddof=1))
    return corr, beta


def _slice(ts, o, c, w, a, b, slip=1.0):
    """Simulate sessions a..b inclusive (both must be trading days)."""
    _, first, last, sess, day_of = _sessions(ts)
    ka, kb = day_of[a], day_of[b]
    i0, i1 = first[ka], last[kb] + 1
    r = bt.simulate(ts[i0:i1], o[i0:i1], c[i0:i1], w[i0:i1],
                    band=BAND, slippage_bps=slip)
    s = bt.stats(r, BARS_PER_YEAR)
    t = ts[i0:i1]
    eq = np.asarray(r["equity"], float)
    deq = pd.Series(eq, index=t).groupby(t.date).last()
    return {
        "cagr": float(s["cagr"]),
        "max_drawdown": float(s["max_drawdown"]),
        "sharpe": float(s["sharpe"]),
        "exposure": float(w[i0:i1, 1].mean()),
        "ending_equity": float(s["ending_equity"]),
    }


def _year_logs(deq):
    ye = deq.groupby(deq.index.map(lambda d: d.year)).last()
    y0 = deq.iloc[0]
    logs, prev = {}, y0
    for y, v in ye.items():
        logs[int(y)] = float(np.log(v / prev))
        prev = v
    return logs

# Main
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
def main():
    ts, o, c = bt.panel(("QQQ", "TQQQ", "BIL"), START, END, "1min", warmup_days=10)
    _, _, _, sess, day_of = _sessions(ts)
    n_sess = len(sess)
    fomc_idx = [k for d in FOMC_DATES if (k := day_of.get(d)) is not None]
    print(f"bars {len(ts):,}  sessions {n_sess}  FOMC {len(fomc_idx)}")

        "agent": "macro-event-tqqq",
        "idea": "Own TQQQ only in the middle of the FOMC intermeeting period; "
                "BIL during the post-decision unwind and the late pre-meeting de-risking.",
        "hypothesis": "The equity risk premium is earned in the ~3 weeks after the "
                      "two-day post-FOMC positioning unwind; the immediate post-decision "
                      "and late pre-meeting phases are flat or negative.",
        "universe": ["QQQ", "TQQQ", "BIL"],

                        "in_panel": len(fomc_idx),
                        "windows_used": len(event_windows(sess, day_of, FOMC_DATES, 3, 20))},
        "excluded": ["unscheduled emergency FOMC 2020-03-03, 2020-03-15",
                     "scheduled 2020-03-18 meeting (cancelled)"],
    }

    # --- benchmark on the same 1-min marks -------------------------------
    i0 = bt.start_index(ts, START)
    bench = bt.benchmark(c[i0:, 1], ts[i0:], BARS_PER_YEAR)
    out["benchmark_1min"] = {k: float(bench[k]) for k in
                             ("cagr", "max_drawdown", "sharpe", "volatility",
                              "years", "ending_equity")}

    # --- primary at 1/5/10 bp -------------------------------------------
    w_primary = build_weights(ts, o, c)
    per_cost = {}
    primary_eq = primary_dts = primary_deq = None
    for slip in COSTS:
        m, eq, dts, deq = _metrics(ts, o, c, w_primary, slip)
        per_cost[f"{slip:.0f}bp"] = m
        if slip == 1.0:
            primary_eq, primary_dts, primary_deq = eq, dts, deq
    corr_t, beta_t = _corr_beta(primary_dts, primary_eq, c[i0:, 1])
    corr_q, beta_q = _corr_beta(primary_dts, primary_eq, c[i0:, 0])
    out["primary"] = {
        "id": "G1",
        "params": {"fomc_window": [3, 20], "hold_sessions": 18},
        "dev": per_cost,
        "corr_tqqq_daily": corr_t,
        "beta_tqqq_daily": beta_t,
        "corr_qqq_daily": corr_q,
        "beta_qqq_daily": beta_q,
    }

    out["windows"] = {"dev": per_cost}
    out["dev_1bp"] = per_cost["1bp"]
    out["exposure"] = per_cost["1bp"]["exposure"]
    out["corr_vs_tqqq"] = corr_t
    out["corr_vs_qqq"] = corr_q
    out["yearly"] = per_cost["1bp"]["yearly"]

    # --- pre-registered grid (8 cells) ----------------------------------
    def cell_windows(fomc_off=(3, 20), extras=()):
        wins = event_windows(sess, day_of, FOMC_DATES, fomc_off[0], fomc_off[1])
        for ev, a, b in extras:
            wins += event_windows(sess, day_of, ev, a, b)
        return wins

    grid_defs = [
        ("G1", (3, 20), (), "primary: middle of the intermeeting period"),
        ("G2", (1, 15), (), "early phase, shorter"),
        ("G3", (3, 15), (), "shorter middle"),
        ("G4", (3, 25), (), "longer middle, includes late pre-meeting"),
        ("G5", (5, 20), (), "later start, more unwind skipped"),
        ("G6", (3, 20), ((CPI_DATES, -1, 2),), "FOMC window + CPI [-1,+2]"),
        ("G7", (3, 20), ((OPEX_DATES, 1, 3),), "FOMC window + OpEx [+1,+3]"),
        ("G8", (3, 20), ((CPI_DATES, -1, 2), (OPEX_DATES, 1, 3)),
         "FOMC + CPI + OpEx"),
    ]
    grid = {}
    for cid, fomc_off, extras, note in grid_defs:
        wins = cell_windows(fomc_off, extras)
        w = weights_from_index_windows(ts, wins)
        m, _, _, _ = _metrics(ts, o, c, w, 1.0)
        rec = {"note": note, "fomc_off": list(fomc_off),
               "extras": [[e.__class__.__name__, a, b] for e, a, b in extras],
               "windows": len(wins), "dev_1bp": m}
        if cid in ("G1", "G7", "G8"):
            for slip in (5.0, 10.0):
                mm, _, _, _ = _metrics(ts, o, c, w, slip)
                rec[f"dev_{slip:.0f}bp"] = mm
        grid[cid] = rec
        print(f"  {cid}: CAGR {m['cagr']*100:6.2f}%  DD {m['max_drawdown']*100:5.2f}%  "
              f"Sh {m['sharpe']:4.2f}  exp {m['exposure']*100:4.1f}%  nwin {len(wins)}")
    out["grid"] = grid

    # --- random-date placebo --------------------------------------------
    rng = np.random.default_rng(11)
    n_ev, hold = len(FOMC_DATES), 18
    draws = 500
    pres = []
    for _ in range(draws):
        starts = rng.integers(0, max(1, n_sess - hold), n_ev)
        wins = [(int(s), int(min(s + hold - 1, n_sess - 1))) for s in starts]
        w = weights_from_index_windows(ts, wins)
        m, _, _, _ = _metrics(ts, o, c, w, 1.0)
        pres.append((m["cagr"], m["max_drawdown"], m["sharpe"], m["exposure"]))
    pres = np.asarray(pres)
    p = per_cost["1bp"]
    out["placebo"] = {
        "draws": draws,
        "n_events": n_ev,
        "hold_sessions": hold,
        "seed": 11,
        "note": "random start sessions, same event count and hold length; overlaps allowed",
        "cagr": {"median": float(np.median(pres[:, 0])),
                 "p90": float(np.percentile(pres[:, 0], 90)),
                 "p95": float(np.percentile(pres[:, 0], 95)),
                 "p99": float(np.percentile(pres[:, 0], 99)),
                 "max": float(pres[:, 0].max()),
                 "percentile_of_primary": float((pres[:, 0] < p["cagr"]).mean())},
        "max_drawdown": {"median": float(np.median(pres[:, 1])),
                         "p10": float(np.percentile(pres[:, 1], 10)),
                         "p05": float(np.percentile(pres[:, 1], 5)),
                         "min": float(pres[:, 1].min()),
                         "percentile_of_primary": float((pres[:, 1] > p["max_drawdown"]).mean())},
        "sharpe": {"median": float(np.median(pres[:, 2])),
                   "p95": float(np.percentile(pres[:, 2], 95)),
                   "max": float(pres[:, 2].max()),
                   "percentile_of_primary": float((pres[:, 2] < p["sharpe"]).mean())},
        "exposure_median": float(np.median(pres[:, 3])),
        "joint_frac_cagr_ge_and_dd_le": float(np.mean(
            (pres[:, 0] >= p["cagr"]) & (pres[:, 1] <= p["max_drawdown"]))),
    }

    # Exposure-matched placebo: a generic 30-session cycle with a random phase.
    # 63 non-overlapping 18-session windows -> roughly the same time in market.
    phase_res = []
    for phase in range(30):
        wins, s = [], phase
        while len(wins) < n_ev and s + hold - 1 < n_sess:
            wins.append((s, s + hold - 1))
            s += 30
        w = weights_from_index_windows(ts, wins)
        m, _, _, _ = _metrics(ts, o, c, w, 1.0)
        phase_res.append((m["cagr"], m["max_drawdown"], m["sharpe"], m["exposure"]))
    phase_res = np.asarray(phase_res)
    out["placebo_phase"] = {
        "note": "generic 30-session cycle, random phase, 63 non-overlapping 18-session "
                "windows; same frequency and roughly the same exposure as the primary",
        "phases": 30,
        "exposure_median": float(np.median(phase_res[:, 3])),
        "cagr": {"median": float(np.median(phase_res[:, 0])),
                 "p90": float(np.percentile(phase_res[:, 0], 90)),
                 "p95": float(np.percentile(phase_res[:, 0], 95)),
                 "max": float(phase_res[:, 0].max()),
                 "percentile_of_primary": float((phase_res[:, 0] < p["cagr"]).mean())},
        "max_drawdown": {"median": float(np.median(phase_res[:, 1])),
                         "p05": float(np.percentile(phase_res[:, 1], 5)),
                         "min": float(phase_res[:, 1].min()),
                         "percentile_of_primary": float((phase_res[:, 1] > p["max_drawdown"]).mean())},
        "sharpe": {"median": float(np.median(phase_res[:, 2])),
                   "p95": float(np.percentile(phase_res[:, 2], 95)),
                   "max": float(phase_res[:, 2].max()),
                   "percentile_of_primary": float((phase_res[:, 2] < p["sharpe"]).mean())},
        "joint_frac_cagr_ge_and_dd_le": float(np.mean(
            (phase_res[:, 0] >= p["cagr"]) & (phase_res[:, 1] <= p["max_drawdown"]))),
    }
    print(f"  phase placebo: CAGR p50 {out['placebo_phase']['cagr']['median']*100:5.1f}%  "
          f"p95 {out['placebo_phase']['cagr']['p95']*100:5.1f}%  primary pct "
          f"{out['placebo_phase']['cagr']['percentile_of_primary']*100:4.1f}%")
    print(f"  placebo: CAGR p50 {out['placebo']['cagr']['median']*100:5.1f}%  "
          f"p95 {out['placebo']['cagr']['p95']*100:5.1f}%  primary pct "
          f"{out['placebo']['cagr']['percentile_of_primary']*100:4.1f}%")

    # --- shifted calendar ------------------------------------------------
    shift_rows = {}
    for shift in range(-15, 16):
        wins = []
        for k in fomc_idx:
            ka, kb = k + shift + 3, k + shift + 20
            if ka < 0 or kb >= n_sess:
                continue
            wins.append((ka, kb))
        w = weights_from_index_windows(ts, wins)
        m, _, _, _ = _metrics(ts, o, c, w, 1.0)
        shift_rows[str(shift)] = {"cagr": m["cagr"], "max_drawdown": m["max_drawdown"],
                                  "sharpe": m["sharpe"], "exposure": m["exposure"]}
    out["shift_test"] = {
        "note": "all FOMC dates shifted by N sessions; same 18-session hold",
        "by_shift": shift_rows,
        "peak_shift": max(shift_rows, key=lambda s: shift_rows[s]["cagr"]),
    }

    # --- cuts ------------------------------------------------------------
    cuts = {}
    for lab, a, b in (("2016-2019", date(2016, 1, 4), date(2019, 12, 31)),
                      ("2020-2021", date(2020, 1, 2), date(2021, 12, 31)),
                      ("2022-2023", date(2022, 1, 3), date(2023, 12, 29))):
        cuts[lab] = _slice(ts, o, c, w_primary, a, b)
    out["cuts"] = {"subperiods": cuts}

    ylogs = _year_logs(primary_deq)
    tot = float(np.log(primary_deq.iloc[-1] / primary_deq.iloc[0]))
    loo = {}
    for y, lg in ylogs.items():
        loo[str(y)] = {"year_return": float(np.exp(lg) - 1.0),
                       "ex_cagr": float(np.exp((tot - lg) / 7.0) - 1.0)}
    out["cuts"]["leave_one_year_out"] = loo

    # --- per-cycle event study ------------------------------------------
    cyc = []
    for k in fomc_idx:
        ka, kb = k + 3, k + 20
        if kb >= n_sess:
            continue
        _, first, last, _, _ = _sessions(ts)
        ia, ib = first[ka], last[kb]
        cyc.append({
            "fomc": str(sess[k]),
            "start": str(sess[ka]),
            "end": str(sess[kb]),
            "tqqq": float(c[ib, 1] / o[ia, 1] - 1.0),
            "qqq": float(c[ib, 0] / o[ia, 0] - 1.0),
            "held_sessions": int(kb - ka + 1),
        })
    tx = np.array([r["tqqq"] for r in cyc])
    qx = np.array([r["qqq"] for r in cyc])
    out["event_study"] = {
        "n_cycles": len(cyc),
        "tqqq": {"mean": float(tx.mean()), "median": float(np.median(tx)),
                 "sd": float(tx.std(ddof=1)),
                 "t": float(tx.mean() / (tx.std(ddof=1) / np.sqrt(len(tx)))),
                 "positive_share": float((tx > 0).mean()),
                 "worst": sorted(cyc, key=lambda r: r["tqqq"])[:5],
                 "best": sorted(cyc, key=lambda r: r["tqqq"])[-5:]},
        "qqq": {"mean": float(qx.mean()), "median": float(np.median(qx)),
                "sd": float(qx.std(ddof=1)),
                "t": float(qx.mean() / (qx.std(ddof=1) / np.sqrt(len(qx)))),
                "positive_share": float((qx > 0).mean())},
    }

    # --- MArch 2020 cancelled-meeting sensitivity ------------------------
    extra = FOMC_DATES + [date(2020, 3, 18)]
    w_alt = weights_from_index_windows(
        ts, event_windows(sess, day_of, extra, 3, 20))
    m_alt, _, _, _ = _metrics(ts, o, c, w_alt, 1.0)
    out["sensitivity_cancelled_mar2020"] = {
        "note": "adds the cancelled 2020-03-18 scheduled date; not used by the primary",
        "dev_1bp": m_alt,
    }

    # --- status ----------------------------------------------------------
    passed = (p["cagr"] > TQQQ_BAR["cagr"]
              and p["max_drawdown"] < TQQQ_BAR["max_drawdown"])
    out["passed_dev_bar"] = bool(passed)
    out["status"] = "passed_dev_only" if passed else "below_dev_bar"
    out["status_note"] = (
        "Development gates only.  The pass is concentrated in 2020 and the "
        "leave-one-year-out ex-2020 CAGR is below the bar; see report.md.  "
        "No holdout was loaded."
    )
    out["notes"] = [
        "TQQQ benchmark recomputed on the same 1-min panel is 36.15% / 82.29% / 0.80; "
        "the program bar is the published 36.72% / 82.29% / 0.82.",
        f"FOMC events: {len(FOMC_DATES)} scheduled, {len(fomc_idx)} in panel, "
        f"{out['event_count']['windows_used']} windows used.",
        "2020 March scheduled meeting was cancelled; emergency meetings are excluded "
        "because they were not knowable in advance.",
        "The +3/+20 boundaries came from a coarse dev offset scan, disclosed in "
        "report.md; the grid is a plateau test, not a selection menu.",
    ]

    (HERE / "result.json").write_text(json.dumps(out, indent=2, default=float),
                                      encoding="utf-8")
    print(f"\nwrote {HERE / 'result.json'}")
    print(f"primary 1bp: CAGR {p['cagr']*100:.2f}%  DD {p['max_drawdown']*100:.2f}%  "
          f"Sharpe {p['sharpe']:.2f}  exposure {p['exposure']*100:.1f}%  "
          f"corr {corr_t:.2f}  fills {p['fills']}  turnover {p['turnover']:.0f}x")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
